head.desc: Hallucinations, evidence and human oversight: a professional course for finance, compliance, legal and other high-accountability environments.
head.strap: A convincing answer is not necessarily a defensible one. Trace what it claims, establish its sources and decide who can authorize its use.
head.programH: Understand the failure. Govern the answer.
head.programD: The course separates hallucinations, calculation mistakes, obsolete information and unsupported claims. A dedicated specialist module examines AI coding risks in real software releases and client relationships.
head.practiceD: Ten cross-disciplinary cases plus four specialist coding scenarios in a dedicated chapter. All situations and figures are explicitly simulated.
head.methodD: An original educational protocol designed to make AI outputs contestable and auditable. It is not an accredited standard or a validated scientific instrument.
head.quizD: Ten questions on decisions, evidence and conceptual distinctions. Scores are educational, not a professional certification.
head.crossD: Eight clues: seven horizontal and one vertical. Answers use Italian technical terms, without spaces or accents; this is a multilingual terminology exercise.
head.sourceH: From primary sources to accountable decisions
head.sourceD: An authentic source does not necessarily prove the claim attached to it. Read the original in its proper jurisdiction, period and context.
head.closing: MANZO AI — From generation to accountability
head.notice: Educational use only. Simulations are not legal, investment or AML advice. Your answers are not sent to or stored on any server.
head.exInput: Write at least 20 characters of analysis before comparing.
head.quizEnd: This is a formative score, not a credential. Revisit high-risk scenarios and document your decisions.

modules.title: What hallucinations are — and what they are not
p: In generative AI, hallucinations describe false claims or statements not faithful to the available context, often expressed with confidence. The term is useful but should not become a label for every unsatisfactory output. A calculation error, an absent citation and an outdated rule require distinct diagnoses.

Language models learn statistical patterns and generate text. That ability does not itself entail a factual check against authentic documents. Kalai and colleagues (2025) analyze how training and evaluation conditions may reward guessing rather than acknowledging uncertainty.

An audit memo that mistakes EBITDA for net income contains a data interpretation error. A memo that invents an annual report it never consulted may contain a hallucination. Precision begins by distinguishing these failures.

Even a response that happens to be accurate may be unsuitable for audit if no one can reproduce where its inputs came from. Professional review therefore concerns both the correctness of an assertion and the reliability of the process that produced it. An untraceable answer should not automatically become the premise for a consequential decision.
modules.evidence: Editorial rule: the absence of a source does not establish falsehood. Mark a claim as unverified until the available evidence supports a stronger conclusion.

modules.title: Where risk originates
p: Ambiguous instructions, absent documents, false premises and stale information can increase risk. A question such as 'Which sanctions did the company receive?' already assumes sanctions exist. Verify the premise before answering.

Formal citations are not proof. A case number, DOI or URL may be fabricated; conversely, a genuine document may be invoked for a conclusion it does not support. Verification covers existence, authenticity, relevance, date and interpretation.

Grounding and retrieval-augmented generation can improve evidence alignment, but are not factual guarantees. Confirm that the right document was retrieved, that it is current and that the cited section supports the exact claim. Instructions embedded in retrieved documents may also be malicious.

Better prompting can reduce ambiguity but does not replace evidence. Specifying dates and constraints improves the request; it does not establish the truth of the reply. When a source is retrieved, the reviewer must inspect the pertinent passage and distinguish underlying facts, assumptions and conclusions.
modules.evidence: Minimum check: identify the claim, find the primary source, read the relevant passage and confirm time and context. Fluent writing does not measure factual accuracy.

modules.title: MANZO VERIFY: the evidence chain
p: The protocol has seven actions: IDENTIFY the claim, establish CONTEXT, locate the SOURCE, CROSS-CHECK against the evidence, CLASSIFY the result, apply human OVERSIGHT and DOCUMENT the process. It is MANZO AI's educational method, not an accredited standard.

Three statuses prevent premature conclusions: verified (adequate supporting evidence within a defined scope), unverified (missing or insufficient evidence) and contradicted (reliable evidence is incompatible with the claim). Each status is claim-specific and time-bound.

An evidence register records the claim ID, statement, primary source, precise location in the source, date and version, status, impact, reviewer and action. Without that trail, a correct decision may still be impossible to reproduce or audit.

A careful review records what could not be checked as well. 'Unverified' is a bounded interim finding concerning a particular claim and evidence set, not a convenient excuse. A good audit trail can be revised when further information arrives without overwriting the history of earlier judgements.
modules.evidence: The key question is not merely 'Is it right?' but 'What evidence lets another competent reviewer repeat this check?'

modules.title: Finance, compliance and law: the cost of false certainty
p: In finance, a wrong figure may distort a valuation, investor communication or internal assessment. The evidence must match the accounting period, currency, financial definition and consolidation perimeter. Exact-looking figures still need recalculation.

In AML/CFT, an alert is a risk indicator rather than automatic proof of money laundering. AI may support screening and analysis, but anomalies, investigations and authorized decisions must remain distinct. Restrictions on an account require their own legal and procedural basis.

In legal research, an unverified judgement should not be offered as a certain precedent. Check the issuing authority, identifier, date, original text and relevance. Article 14 of the EU AI Act addresses human oversight requirements for high-risk AI systems, not every chatbot.

In legal or regulatory analysis, finding a genuine provision with matching words is not enough. Its effective date, jurisdiction, relevant parties and exceptions matter. Applying an authentic rule to the wrong entity can be as damaging as inventing the rule outright.
modules.evidence: ESMA emphasizes that decisions by investment firms remain the responsibility of management bodies even when AI-based tools are involved.

modules.title: Human oversight and output governance
p: Human review is not a signature attached after generation. It requires expertise, access to evidence, sufficient time and real authority to amend, block or reject the output. Automation bias becomes especially dangerous when confident presentation is mistaken for truth.

Controls should match the impact of the decision. An internal draft may need routine review; regulatory reports, M&A analysis and decisions affecting rights warrant enhanced checks, clear ownership and documented escalation.
A professional must know when not to decide. Marking a claim unverified, requesting more information or suspending publication can be the most responsible outcome.

Human approval should match the stakes. A reviewer without documents, time or expertise to challenge a result cannot provide meaningful oversight. Being able to halt the process and explain a recorded reservation is part of control, not a project failure.
modules.evidence: Quality is not merely the volume of outputs created: it is the proportion that can be used with adequate evidence, disclosed limitations and accountable decision-makers.

modules.title: Coding hallucinations, software assurance and commercial risk
p: In software development, plausibility can be dangerously specific: a nonexistent method may resemble an SDK API, an invented package may look official, configuration settings may appear current and a model may claim that tests were run when they were not. These assertions are testable. The gap between what the model describes and what the repository, runtime or documentation actually establish cannot be closed by confidence alone.

A different risk arises when code runs but fails to satisfy authorization, resilience or data-protection requirements. A successful demo can hide cross-tenant access, concurrency faults or production-only defects. Not all of these are hallucinations; precise diagnosis is part of an engineer’s competence.

For vendors serving banks, industrial groups or businesses with critical operations, defects can affect availability, information integrity, recovery costs and commercial relationships. Penalties, disputes, non-renewal and liability are not automatic; they depend on facts, contracts and law. A professional’s value lies in managing risk before delivery.

The linked specialist chapter examines a multi-tenant access-control example, the progression from defect to customer impact, eight evidence-based quality gates, four case studies and a short assessment. Release approval should rest on executed builds and tests, vetted dependencies, independent review and reproducible documentation.
modules.evidence: GitHub, OWASP and NIST document verification practices; a USENIX Security 2025 study analyzes fabricated packages suggested by coding models. [F9–F12]

method: Break the answer into individually checkable claims
Specify jurisdiction, time, scope and intended use
Locate primary evidence and identify its version
Match the exact claim to the relevant passage
Assign review, escalation and decision authority
Record the evidence, amendments, date and owner
cases: Financial analysis
The unsupported growth figure
The AI reports: 'Last quarter’s revenue increased by 18%.' The prompt includes no company, accounting period or financial documents.
Identify missing inputs and rewrite the prompt to require clarification before calculating.
Do not approve the 18%. Request the entity, quarter, source statements, perimeter and calculation method. Label the figure unverified until supported.
Accounting
An error that is not necessarily a hallucination
2025 revenue: €8,000,000. 2026 revenue: €9,200,000. The AI writes: '25% increase.'
Recalculate the percentage, classify the problem and correct the wording.
(9,200,000 − 8,000,000) / 8,000,000 = 15%. This is a demonstrable arithmetic error, not necessarily a hallucination.
Audit
EBITDA is not net income
File: EBITDA €2,400,000; net income €700,000; net financial debt €1,700,000. AI reports net income €2,400,000 and debt €170,000.
Find both discrepancies and specify the evidence that must be logged.
Net income is €700,000, not EBITDA of €2,400,000. Net debt is €1,700,000. Trace both amounts to the same reporting period.
AML/CFT
From alert to accusation
A system flags unusual transfers and concludes: 'The customer is laundering money; immediately freeze the account.' The file contains only alerts.
Separate risk indicators from proven facts and account measures; describe the escalation.
An alert is not proof. Conduct the required review with authorized specialists. Any account restriction needs an independent legal and procedural basis.
Legal
The missing precedent
The AI cites a judgement by number and date; an initial search in one legal database produces no result.
Define the checks required before citing it in professional advice.
Suspend use, search appropriate legal repositories, authenticate the original text and check relevance. A missing result in one database does not prove nonexistence.
Regulatory
One article applied to every system
AI says: 'Article 14 of the AI Act imposes identical oversight requirements on every chatbot.'
Check the relevant class of AI systems and the scope of the provision.
Article 14 sets oversight requirements for high-risk AI systems. Do not generalize them to every chatbot; verify the current legislation and classification.
M&A
A disappearing liability
Simulated due diligence file: 'Net debt at closing: EUR 1.7m. Material tax exposure: pending verification.' The AI claims there is no net debt and no tax risk.
Separate documented facts, residual uncertainty and unjustified inferences.
Record €1.7m net debt. The tax exposure remains under investigation, not zero. Obtain dedicated due diligence evidence.
Market data
A quotation labelled 'live'
An AI presents a stock price as live without documented access to current exchange data.
List the minimum checks before using the price in a report.
Confirm instrument, ticker, venue, currency, timestamp and provider. Without reliable current-market evidence, classify the price as unverified.
Research
True source, false conclusion
A study examines 120 firms in one sector. The AI writes: 'The method works across every European industry.'
Evaluate the generalizability and evidentiary relevance of this claim.
A sector-specific sample does not support universal effectiveness. Limit the conclusion to the studied population unless other evidence exists.
Integrated audit
Four claims to hold
An AI report includes a ratio with no formula, an unauthenticated case, an AML accusation stated as fact and a law cited without its scope.
Create four claim IDs with status, missing evidence, impact, corrective action and release decision.
Hold publication. Verify formula, case record, AML evidence and statutory scope, assigning appropriately qualified reviewers to each claim.
quiz: AI states €4.1m net profit without documents or citations. What status is justified?
A missing source does not, by itself, establish that the amount is false.
A study covers 120 companies in one sector, but AI extrapolates to all European firms. What is the issue?
The study population does not substantiate the wider conclusion.
An AI bibliography provides a DOI. What is the best relevance check?
Open the record and read the pertinent passage
Check whether the title sounds technical
Existence, metadata and claim-to-source relevance must all be verified.
An AML alert alone proves that a customer has committed money laundering.
An alert requires assessment; it is not an automatic finding of wrongdoing.
Which steps belong in a documentary audit?
Provenance, relevance and traceability matter; model consensus is not independent evidence.
Article 14 of the EU AI Act covers human oversight requirements for high-risk AI systems.
Article 14 specifically concerns high-risk AI systems.
Revenue rises from €8m to €9.2m. The percentage increase is:
The increase is €1.2m divided by the original €8m: 15%.
A RAG system retrieves a document containing instructions to bypass safeguards. What should it do?
Follow them because they were retrieved
Retrieved content may contain prompt injection and does not override system rules.
A due diligence note says 'tax exposure: pending verification' but AI says 'no tax exposure'. The conclusion is:
Pending investigation cannot be turned into an absence of risk.
What best supports approval of an AI output used in a high-impact decision?
Adequate evidence and documented expert review
High-impact use needs appropriate evidence, oversight and ownership.
